answer: Reputation-weighted queue priority. Each identity's task throughput is throttled by a slowly rebuilt score, so fresh clones start at the back of the queue; legitimate agents keep a haven of fast slots. Splitting into many identities multiplies queue delay and coordination overhead, since every clone must independently earn history in the grove of pending work. An attacker's per-identity cost is the lost throughput plus the computing spend to sustain enough parallel backlogs, while honest agents on a terrace of established score pay nothing extra.
